Risk: Collateral securing loans is not perfected, revalued or released correctly, overstating security and understating expected credit loss.
Control objective: Ensure collateral is legally perfected, periodically revalued and released only when the exposure is repaid.
Control description: Collateral is recorded in the collateral system only once legal perfection is evidenced by the Legal team; revaluations are performed at the frequency set by asset class using independent valuation sources, and releases require approval by Credit Risk independent of the relationship manager.
Segregation of duties: The relationship manager cannot record, revalue or release collateral.
Test of design: Inspect the collateral procedure, perfection checklist, revaluation frequency table and release workflow.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of secured facilities; agree perfection evidence, latest revaluation and, for released collateral, approval and repayment.
Population / evidence source: Secured facilities and collateral releases in the period

Risk: Loan proceeds are disbursed to an account other than the approved borrower account, or before conditions precedent are satisfied.
Control objective: Ensure disbursement occurs only after conditions precedent are met and only to the approved account.
Control description: Loan Operations verifies that all conditions precedent recorded in the credit approval are satisfied and that the disbursement account matches the approved borrower account before release; disbursement is authorised by two officers independent of credit origination.
Segregation of duties: Credit origination staff cannot execute or authorise disbursement.
Test of design: Inspect the disbursement checklist, condition precedent tracking and dual authorisation configuration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of disbursements; agree to satisfied conditions precedent, the approved account and dual authorisation.
Population / evidence source: All loan disbursements in the period

Risk: Deteriorating loans are not migrated to the correct stage or classification, deferring impairment recognition.
Control objective: Ensure loans are classified and staged in accordance with policy and observable credit deterioration indicators.
Control description: The system applies staging rules based on days past due and qualitative deterioration triggers; monthly, Credit Risk reviews the staging migration report and all manual overrides of system-assigned staging require Credit Committee approval with documented rationale.
Segregation of duties: Relationship managers cannot override staging assigned by the system.
Test of design: Inspect the staging rule configuration, override workflow and Credit Committee terms of reference.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform staging from days past due data and inspect approval of all overrides.
Population / evidence source: Monthly staging migration reports and override approvals

Risk: Interest and fees are accrued on non-performing exposures or calculated on incorrect terms, overstating income.
Control objective: Ensure interest and fee income is recognised on correct terms and ceases on non-performing exposures.
Control description: The core banking system calculates interest from contracted terms and suspends accrual automatically on classification as non-performing; monthly, Financial Control reconciles interest income to the loan book and reviews an exception report of manually adjusted accruals.
Segregation of duties: Staff maintaining loan terms cannot post manual interest adjustments.
Test of design: Inspect the accrual configuration, non-accrual suspension logic and reconciliation template.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the interest reconciliation and test manual adjustments to approval.

Risk: Loans are restructured to avoid recognising default, so forbearance is not identified and impairment is understated.
Control objective: Ensure modifications are identified as forbearance where applicable and are approved and disclosed correctly.
Control description: All loan modifications are assessed against forbearance criteria by Credit Risk independent of the relationship manager, approved at the authority level set by exposure, and flagged in the system so that staging and disclosure reflect the modification.
Segregation of duties: The relationship manager proposing the modification cannot assess or approve its forbearance classification.
Test of design: Inspect the forbearance assessment criteria, approval matrix and system flagging.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of modifications; agree the forbearance assessment, approval and system flag.
Population / evidence source: All loan modifications in the period

Risk: Loans are written off without authority to remove problem exposures from reporting, or recoveries are misappropriated.
Control objective: Ensure write-offs are authorised at the correct level and recoveries are completely recorded.
Control description: Write-offs require approval at the authority level set by exposure size, with evidence that recovery avenues have been exhausted; recoveries on written-off accounts are received into a designated account, reconciled monthly by Financial Control and reported to the Credit Committee.
Segregation of duties: Recovery collection staff do not authorise write-offs or reconcile recovery receipts.
Test of design: Inspect the write-off authority matrix, recovery reconciliation and committee reporting.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of write-offs; agree approval and recovery evidence. Reconcile recoveries received to the ledger for a sample of months.
Population / evidence source: Write-offs and post write-off recoveries in the period

Risk: Accounts are opened without complete customer due diligence, breaching regulation and enabling illicit funds to enter the bank.
Control objective: Ensure accounts are opened only where identification and due diligence requirements are satisfied.
Control description: The onboarding workflow prevents account activation until identification, verification and risk rating are complete; enhanced due diligence for high-risk customers requires approval by Financial Crime Compliance independent of the relationship.
Segregation of duties: Relationship staff cannot approve their own enhanced due diligence or override risk ratings.
Test of design: Inspect the onboarding workflow configuration and enhanced due diligence approval routing.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of accounts opened; agree due diligence completeness, risk rating and any EDD approval.
Population / evidence source: All accounts opened during the period

Risk: Interest paid on customer deposits is calculated on incorrect rates or balances, misstating interest expense and customer balances.
Control objective: Ensure deposit interest is calculated in accordance with product terms and approved rate tables.
Control description: Rate tables are maintained by Product Control and independently verified before activation; monthly, Financial Control recalculates interest on a risk-based sample of products and reconciles total interest expense to the deposit book.
Segregation of duties: The preparer of the rate table does not approve its activation.
Test of design: Inspect the rate maintenance procedure and the monthly recalculation and reconciliation.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the interest recalculation and agree the expense to the ledger.

Risk: Dormant accounts are reactivated fraudulently, or unclaimed balances are not escheated as required by regulation.
Control objective: Ensure dormant balances are protected from unauthorised access and escheated in accordance with law.
Control description: Accounts meeting the dormancy criteria are automatically blocked from transacting; reactivation requires customer identity verification and approval by a manager independent of branch operations, and unclaimed balances are reported and remitted to the authority on the statutory timetable.
Segregation of duties: Branch staff who request reactivation cannot approve it.
Test of design: Inspect the dormancy configuration, reactivation approval workflow and escheatment procedure.
Test of operating effectiveness: Test all reactivations in the period for verification and approval; agree escheatment to statutory deadlines.
Population / evidence source: Dormant account reactivations and escheatment submissions

Risk: Customer fees are applied that are not permitted by the product terms, generating remediation liabilities and regulatory censure.
Control objective: Ensure fees charged to customers are permitted, correctly calculated and disclosed.
Control description: Fee configuration changes require approval by Product Control and Compliance before activation; monthly, an exception report of manual fee applications and waivers is reviewed by the Head of Operations, and fee income is reconciled to the fee schedule.
Segregation of duties: Branch staff applying manual fees do not maintain the fee configuration.
Test of design: Inspect the fee change approval process and the manual fee exception report.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the fee reconciliation and test manual applications and waivers for approval.
Population / evidence source: Monthly fee reconciliations and manual fee reports

Risk: A sanctioned party transacts through the bank because screening lists are stale or matches are cleared without proper review.
Control objective: Ensure customers and payments are screened against current sanctions lists and that matches are properly adjudicated.
Control description: Sanctions lists are updated automatically on publication and screening runs on every customer at onboarding, on the full base after each list update, and on every cross-border payment before release; potential matches are adjudicated by Financial Crime Compliance, not by the business, with dual review on discounted true-match candidates.
Segregation of duties: Business and operations staff cannot discount a screening alert.
Test of design: Inspect the screening configuration, list update mechanism and alert adjudication workflow.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform screening on a sample of customers and payments to confirm expected hits; test a sample of discounted alerts for reviewer independence and rationale.
Population / evidence source: Screening alerts raised during the period

Risk: Suspicious activity is not detected because monitoring scenarios are not tuned to the bank's risk profile or alerts are closed without investigation.
Control objective: Ensure transaction monitoring scenarios are appropriate, operating and producing investigated outcomes.
Control description: Monitoring scenarios are reviewed and tuned at least annually against the enterprise financial crime risk assessment with results approved by the Financial Crime Committee; alerts are investigated within defined timeframes and closure rationale is subject to quality assurance sampling by a team independent of the investigators.
Segregation of duties: Quality assurance reviewers are independent of the analysts whose closures they test.
Test of design: Inspect the scenario tuning methodology, committee approval and the quality assurance process.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of periods, inspect tuning evidence; sample closed alerts and reassess the adequacy of the closure rationale.
Population / evidence source: Alerts closed during the period and annual tuning documentation

Risk: Suspicious activity reports are filed late or not at all, breaching statutory obligations and exposing the bank to enforcement.
Control objective: Ensure suspicious activity is escalated, decided and reported within statutory deadlines.
Control description: Escalations are logged on receipt and the Money Laundering Reporting Officer records a documented decision to report or not report within the internal deadline; filings are tracked against the statutory timetable and overdue items are escalated to the Financial Crime Committee monthly.
Segregation of duties: The MLRO decision is independent of the business relationship generating the escalation.
Test of design: Inspect the escalation log, decision documentation standard and deadline tracking.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of escalations, agree the decision documentation and measure elapsed time to filing against the statutory deadline.
Population / evidence source: Internal escalations and filed reports in the period

Risk: Regulatory liquidity ratios are misstated because the classification of assets and outflow assumptions are applied incorrectly.
Control objective: Ensure regulatory liquidity ratios are calculated on correct classifications and approved assumptions.
Control description: Monthly, Treasury Reporting calculates the liquidity ratios and an independent review by Risk Control verifies asset classification, haircuts and outflow factors against the regulatory rules before submission; the Asset and Liability Committee reviews the results.
Segregation of duties: The preparer of the ratio calculation is independent of the reviewer in Risk Control.
Test of design: Inspect the calculation methodology, classification rules and evidence of independent review.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the ratio calculation from source data and inspect the review evidence.
Population / evidence source: Monthly liquidity ratio calculations and submissions

Risk: Securities are valued using stale or unverified prices, misstating the investment portfolio and capital.
Control objective: Ensure securities are valued using independently verified prices at the appropriate fair value level.
Control description: Monthly, an independent price verification is performed by Risk Control against external sources for all portfolio holdings; level 3 valuations require model validation and Valuation Committee approval, and price exceptions above tolerance are escalated before month end close.
Segregation of duties: Front office cannot supply the prices used for independent verification.
Test of design: Inspect the price verification methodology, tolerance thresholds and Valuation Committee terms of reference.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform price verification on a sample of holdings and inspect resolution of exceptions.

Sub-process: Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book
Risk: Interest rate risk is understated because behavioural assumptions on non-maturity deposits and prepayment are not validated.
Control objective: Ensure interest rate risk measurement uses validated assumptions and remains within approved limits.
Control description: Behavioural assumptions for non-maturity deposits and prepayment are validated at least annually against observed customer behaviour by Model Risk, and quarterly the Asset and Liability Committee reviews interest rate risk measures against board-approved limits with breaches escalated.
Segregation of duties: Model owners in Treasury are separate from the Model Risk validation function.
Test of design: Inspect the assumption validation methodology and ALCO limit framework.
Test of operating effectiveness: Obtain the most recent validation; re-perform the assumption back-test and inspect ALCO escalation of breaches.
Population / evidence source: Annual assumption validations and quarterly ALCO packs

Risk: Loans are advanced to borrowers who do not meet credit policy, or on terms outside delegated lending authority, leading to elevated default and impairment.
Control objective: Ensure credit is granted only within approved policy and delegated lending authority.
Control description: Every credit application is scored and reviewed against the credit policy by an underwriter independent of the relationship manager, and approved at the authority level set by exposure size in the delegated lending authority matrix before funds are released.
Segregation of duties: The relationship manager who originates the application cannot approve it or release the funds.
Test of design: Inspect the credit policy, delegated authority matrix and origination workflow to confirm system-enforced approval limits.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of loans advanced; agree the approval to the authority matrix and inspect the independent underwriting assessment.
Population / evidence source: All loans advanced during the period

Risk: The expected credit loss allowance is understated because staging criteria, macroeconomic scenarios or post-model overlays are not applied consistently.
Control objective: Ensure the ECL allowance is calculated using approved models, inputs and overlays, and is subject to independent review.
Control description: Quarterly, the Model Risk function independently validates ECL model outputs, staging migration and scenario weightings, and all management overlays are documented, quantified and approved by the Provisions Committee before the allowance is booked.
Segregation of duties: Model owners in Credit Risk are separate from the Model Risk validation function.
Test of design: Inspect the model governance framework, validation reports and Provisions Committee terms of reference.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, agree the booked allowance to the approved committee paper and re-perform the overlay calculation.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly ECL calculations, validation reports and committee minutes

Risk: Risk-weighted assets are misclassified, misstating the regulatory capital ratio reported to the regulator.
Control objective: Ensure exposures are assigned the correct risk weight and capital returns reconcile to the general ledger.
Control description: Monthly, the Regulatory Reporting Manager reconciles the capital return to the general ledger and to the source exposure systems, and reviews a risk-weight assignment exception report before the Chief Financial Officer signs the return.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the return does not approve or submit it.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template, the exception report logic and the sign-off protocol.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the reconciliation and inspect resolution of risk-weight exceptions.
Population / evidence source: Monthly regulatory capital returns and reconciliations

Risk: Unreconciled items in suspense and nostro accounts conceal misappropriation or processing errors.
Control objective: Ensure suspense and nostro accounts are reconciled and aged items are cleared and investigated.
Control description: Daily nostro and suspense reconciliations are prepared by Operations and reviewed by a supervisor; items ageing beyond 30 days are escalated monthly to the Financial Controller with a documented clearance plan.
Segregation of duties: The preparer of the reconciliation cannot post clearing entries without independent review.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation procedure, ageing report and escalation protocol.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of days, inspect the reconciliation and supervisory review; test the ageing report for items cleared without support.

Risk: Fraudulent or duplicate claims are settled, or claims are paid outside the handler's settlement authority.
Control objective: Ensure claims are validated against policy cover and settled within delegated authority.
Control description: Each claim is validated against policy cover and the claims system enforces settlement authority by value; claims above the handler limit require review by a claims manager, and all settlements are screened against duplicate and fraud indicator rules before payment release.
Segregation of duties: The handler who assesses the claim cannot release the payment.
Test of design: Inspect the settlement authority configuration and the fraud rule set in the claims system.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of settled claims; agree the settlement to policy cover, authority limit and evidence of fraud screening.
Population / evidence source: All claims settled during the period

Risk: Reserves for incurred but not reported claims are understated through inappropriate development factors or unsupported management adjustments.
Control objective: Ensure technical reserves are actuarially determined, independently reviewed and adjusted only with documented justification.
Control description: Quarterly, the Appointed Actuary calculates reserves using approved methodology; results are peer-reviewed by an independent actuary, and any management adjustment to the actuarial central estimate is documented and approved by the Reserving Committee.
Segregation of duties: The reserving actuary is independent of underwriting and claims settlement.
Test of design: Inspect the reserving methodology, peer review protocol and Reserving Committee terms of reference.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, agree booked reserves to the actuarial report and inspect approval of any management adjustment.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly actuarial reserve reports and committee minutes

Risk: Premium is recognised on binding rather than over the policy period, overstating earned premium and understating the unearned premium reserve.
Control objective: Ensure premium is earned over the period of cover and the unearned premium reserve is complete.
Control description: Monthly, the Financial Reporting Manager reconciles written premium from the policy administration system to the general ledger and recalculates the unearned premium reserve on a pro-rata basis, with Controller review of the movement against policy volumes.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the reserve calculation is independent of underwriting.
Test of design: Inspect the earning methodology and evidence of Controller review.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform the unearned premium calculation for a sample of months and agree to the ledger.
Population / evidence source: Monthly premium reconciliations and UPR calculations

Risk: Reinsurance recoveries are not claimed on qualifying losses, or are recognised against treaties that do not cover the loss.
Control objective: Ensure reinsurance recoveries recognised are complete, valid and collectable.
Control description: Quarterly, the Reinsurance Manager reconciles ceded losses to treaty terms and to reinsurer confirmations, reviews recovery ageing and reinsurer credit ratings, and the Controller approves any provision against doubtful recoveries.
Segregation of duties: Recovery calculation and provision approval are performed by different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation approach, ageing review and credit assessment procedure.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, agree recoveries to treaty terms and reinsurer confirmations.

Risk: Standard costs are not updated for input price and yield changes, so inventory is misvalued and variances absorb the error.
Control objective: Ensure standard costs remain supportable and material variances are analysed and resolved.
Control description: Annually the Cost Accounting Manager rolls standard costs using current material, labour and overhead rates with Controller approval; monthly, purchase price and usage variances are analysed by cost centre and explanations above threshold are documented and reviewed.
Segregation of duties: Standard cost changes are approved by someone other than the preparer.
Test of design: Inspect the standard cost roll procedure, threshold definition and variance review template.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform variance calculations and inspect documented explanations and review.
Population / evidence source: Monthly variance analyses and the annual standard cost roll

Risk: Recorded inventory quantities differ from physical stock because counts are infrequent, poorly controlled, or adjustments are posted without approval.
Control objective: Ensure inventory quantities are verified by count and adjustments are authorised.
Control description: Cycle counts are performed to a risk-based schedule covering all A-class items quarterly; counters are independent of stores custody, variances above tolerance are recounted, and all inventory adjustments require Plant Controller approval before posting.
Segregation of duties: Count teams are independent of warehouse custody; the person recounting is not the original counter.
Test of design: Inspect the cycle count programme, coverage schedule and adjustment approval workflow.
Test of operating effectiveness: Attend a count; for a sample of periods, agree count sheets to system adjustments and inspect approval.
Population / evidence source: Cycle count records and inventory adjustment postings

Risk: Provision for obsolete and slow-moving inventory is understated because ageing data is inaccurate or engineering change notices are not reflected.
Control objective: Ensure the inventory provision reflects ageing, demand and product lifecycle status.
Control description: Quarterly, Supply Chain and Finance jointly review the inventory ageing and slow-moving report against forecast demand and engineering change notices, and the resulting provision is approved by the Controller.
Segregation of duties: Supply chain proposes the provision; Finance independently reviews and approves it.
Test of design: Inspect the provision policy, ageing report logic and evidence of joint review.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, re-perform the provision using the ageing report and inspect approval.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly inventory provision calculations and ageing reports

Risk: The warranty provision does not reflect emerging failure rates or an announced recall, understating liabilities.
Control objective: Ensure the warranty provision reflects current claims experience and known product issues.
Control description: Quarterly, the Quality Director provides failure rate and claims data by product line to Finance, which recalculates the warranty provision; recalls and known field issues are separately assessed and approved by the Controller.
Segregation of duties: Quality data provider is independent of the finance preparer of the provision.
Test of design: Inspect the provision methodology and the process for capturing field issues and recalls.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, recompute the provision from claims data and inspect Controller approval.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly warranty provision calculations and quality claims data

Risk: Store cash takings are misappropriated or short-banked, concealed through unauthorised voids, refunds and no-sale transactions.
Control objective: Ensure store takings are complete, banked intact and reconciled to point-of-sale records.
Control description: Daily, the store manager reconciles till readings to cash counted and to the banking slip; voids, refunds and no-sale transactions above threshold require supervisor authorisation at the till, and head office reviews an exception report of till variances and refund patterns by store weekly.
Segregation of duties: The cashier operating the till does not perform the end-of-day count alone; banking is verified independently at head office.
Test of design: Inspect the daily reconciliation procedure, till authorisation configuration and the weekly exception report.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of store-days, agree till readings to counted cash and bank credit; review exception report follow-up.
Population / evidence source: Daily store cash reconciliations and weekly exception reports

Risk: Supplier rebates are recognised before the earning conditions are met, overstating margin.
Control objective: Ensure rebate income is recognised only when the contractual conditions are satisfied and is supported by agreements.
Control description: Quarterly, the Commercial Finance Manager reconciles accrued rebates to signed supplier agreements and purchase volumes, and material rebates are confirmed with the supplier before recognition; the Controller reviews and approves the rebate accrual.
Segregation of duties: Buyers who negotiate rebates do not calculate or approve the accrual.
Test of design: Inspect the rebate recognition policy, agreement repository and confirmation process.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, agree accrued rebates to signed agreements and volume data; inspect supplier confirmations.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly rebate accruals and supplier agreements

Risk: Inventory shrinkage from theft, process error or supplier short-delivery is absorbed into cost of sales without identification or correction.
Control objective: Ensure shrinkage is measured by store, investigated and reflected in the financial statements.
Control description: Stores are counted at least twice a year by an independent count provider; shrinkage is calculated by store and category, stores above the shrinkage threshold are subject to a loss-prevention review, and the shrinkage accrual between counts is approved by the Controller.
Segregation of duties: Count provider is independent of store management whose results are being measured.
Test of design: Inspect the count programme, shrinkage calculation and loss-prevention escalation criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of stores, agree count results to system adjustments; inspect escalation for stores above threshold.
Population / evidence source: Store count results and shrinkage accrual calculations

Risk: Gift card and loyalty liabilities are understated, or breakage is recognised without a supportable redemption history.
Control objective: Ensure gift card and loyalty obligations are completely recorded and breakage is supportable.
Control description: Monthly, the Revenue Accountant reconciles the gift card and loyalty liability to the issuing platform, and breakage is recognised only using the redemption pattern approved annually by the Controller and revisited against actual redemption experience.
Segregation of duties: The person maintaining the loyalty platform does not approve the breakage assumption.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation, the breakage methodology and evidence of annual reassessment.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the reconciliation and recompute breakage on the approved basis.
Population / evidence source: Monthly liability reconciliations and the annual breakage assessment

Risk: Revenue is recognised on ticket sale rather than on flight, overstating revenue and understating the unflown ticket liability.
Control objective: Ensure passenger revenue is recognised when the flight is flown and the air traffic liability is complete.
Control description: Monthly, the Revenue Accounting Manager reconciles tickets sold, flown, refunded and expired from the revenue accounting system to the air traffic liability in the general ledger, and the Controller reviews the liability movement and the expiry recognition against the approved policy.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the liability reconciliation is independent of sales and distribution.
Test of design: Inspect the revenue recognition policy and the air traffic liability reconciliation template.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the reconciliation and agree flown revenue to flight coupon data.

Risk: Ground handling services performed for airline customers are not billed, or are billed below the contracted tariff.
Control objective: Ensure all ground handling services performed are captured and billed at contracted rates.
Control description: The station reconciles daily service delivery records to flight movement data, and the billing system prices services from the contracted tariff table; the Station Manager reviews an unbilled services report weekly and approves manual rate overrides.
Segregation of duties: Staff recording service delivery do not maintain the tariff table.
Test of design: Inspect the service capture process, tariff configuration and unbilled report.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of weeks, reconcile flight movements to services billed and re-price a sample of invoices to contract.
Population / evidence source: Weekly service delivery and billing reconciliations

Risk: Provisions for scheduled airframe and engine overhauls on leased aircraft are misstated because utilisation or overhaul cost assumptions are outdated.
Control objective: Ensure maintenance provisions reflect actual utilisation and current overhaul cost estimates.
Control description: Quarterly, Engineering supplies flight hours and cycles by aircraft and the latest overhaul cost estimates; Finance recalculates the maintenance provision per lease terms and the Controller approves changes to the cost assumption.
Segregation of duties: Engineering provides utilisation data; Finance independently calculates and Controller approves.
Test of design: Inspect the provisioning methodology against lease return conditions and the assumption approval process.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, recompute the provision using utilisation data and approved cost assumptions.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly maintenance provision calculations and utilisation reports

Risk: Fuel hedge accounting is applied to instruments that do not qualify, or hedge positions exceed the mandate approved by the board.
Control objective: Ensure fuel hedging operates within the approved mandate and hedge accounting is properly supported.
Control description: Monthly, Treasury reports open hedge positions against the board-approved mandate limits, and hedge effectiveness testing and documentation are prepared by Financial Reporting and reviewed by the Controller before hedge accounting is applied.
Segregation of duties: The dealer executing hedges does not perform effectiveness testing or confirm positions.
Test of design: Inspect the treasury mandate, hedge documentation standard and effectiveness testing methodology.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, agree open positions to the mandate and inspect effectiveness testing documentation.
Population / evidence source: Monthly hedge position reports and effectiveness testing files

Risk: Room revenue is lost through unauthorised rate discounts, comped rooms and unrecorded occupancy at the front desk.
Control objective: Ensure rooms occupied are recorded and billed at authorised rates.
Control description: The property management system restricts discount and complimentary room codes to authorised users; the Night Auditor reconciles rooms physically occupied to rooms billed each night, and the General Manager reviews a daily exception report of comps, rate overrides and zero-rate stays.
Segregation of duties: The front desk agent granting a rate override cannot approve their own override.
Test of design: Inspect user rights over rate codes and the night audit reconciliation procedure.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of nights, agree occupied rooms to rooms billed and inspect GM review of the exception report.
Population / evidence source: Nightly night-audit packs and exception reports

Risk: Food and beverage stock is consumed without sale through theft, over-pouring or unrecorded staff consumption.
Control objective: Ensure food and beverage cost of sales reflects genuine sales and variances are investigated.
Control description: Monthly, the Food and Beverage Controller counts stock, calculates theoretical versus actual cost of sales by outlet, and outlets exceeding the variance tolerance are investigated with the outlet manager and reported to the General Manager.
Segregation of duties: The person counting stock is independent of the outlet whose variance is being measured.
Test of design: Inspect the costing methodology, tolerance thresholds and investigation protocol.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the theoretical cost calculation and inspect investigation of outlier outlets.
Population / evidence source: Monthly stock counts and cost variance reports

Risk: Advance deposits and loyalty point liabilities are not recognised, understating liabilities and overstating revenue.
Control objective: Ensure advance deposits and loyalty obligations are recorded until the stay is delivered.
Control description: Monthly, the Financial Controller reconciles the advance deposit and loyalty liability accounts to the property management and loyalty systems, and reviews the ageing of deposits held for stays that have already passed.
Segregation of duties: Reconciliation preparer does not process deposit refunds.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the ageing review of expired deposits.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the reconciliation and test the release of aged deposits to revenue.

Risk: Refurbishment spend is capitalised when it is repair in nature, or project costs exceed approved budgets without escalation.
Control objective: Ensure property capital expenditure is authorised, correctly classified and monitored against budget.
Control description: Each capital project is approved against a business case at the authority level set by value; monthly, the Project Accountant reports actual against approved spend, and the Controller reviews the capital versus repairs classification for material additions before posting.
Segregation of duties: Project managers requesting spend do not approve capitalisation treatment.
Test of design: Inspect the capital approval framework and the classification review process.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of additions, agree to approval, inspect the classification assessment and agree spend to budget.
Population / evidence source: Capital additions and monthly project reports

Risk: Amounts collected by payment providers do not reconcile to orders recorded, so revenue and cash are misstated and shortfalls go undetected.
Control objective: Ensure all customer orders are matched to settled funds and differences are investigated.
Control description: Daily, the Revenue Operations Analyst reconciles order value in the commerce platform to gateway settlement reports and to bank credits, and unmatched items are aged and escalated to the Financial Controller weekly.
Segregation of duties: The person performing the reconciliation cannot post adjustments without review.
Test of design: Inspect the three-way reconciliation design between platform, gateway and bank.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of days, re-perform the reconciliation and inspect resolution of unmatched items.

Risk: Fraudulent orders are fulfilled and later charged back, and losses are absorbed without adjusting fraud screening rules.
Control objective: Ensure fraud screening operates effectively and chargeback losses are monitored and acted on.
Control description: Orders are scored by the fraud screening engine before fulfilment, with holds above the risk threshold reviewed manually; monthly, the Risk Manager analyses chargeback reason codes and rates by channel and reports rule changes to the Financial Controller.
Segregation of duties: Manual release of held orders is performed by risk staff, not by sales or fulfilment.
Test of design: Inspect the screening rule set, threshold configuration and manual review workflow.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of released high-risk orders and inspect the documented review; recompute chargeback rates.
Population / evidence source: Held-order review records and monthly chargeback analyses

Risk: Refunds are issued without the goods being returned, or are issued to accounts other than the original payment method.
Control objective: Ensure refunds are issued only for validated returns and to the original payment method.
Control description: The commerce platform restricts refunds to the original payment method and requires a matched return receipt in the warehouse system; refunds without a matched return require supervisor approval, and a daily exception report of these is reviewed by the Customer Operations Manager.
Segregation of duties: Agents issuing refunds cannot amend the return receipt record.
Test of design: Inspect the refund workflow configuration and the exception approval path.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of refunds; agree to matched returns or documented supervisor approval.
Population / evidence source: All refunds issued in the period

Risk: Marketplace seller settlements are calculated on incorrect commission or fee terms, misstating net revenue and seller payables.
Control objective: Ensure marketplace settlements reflect contracted commission and fee terms.
Control description: Monthly, the Marketplace Finance Analyst recalculates a risk-based sample of seller settlements against contracted commission rates and reconciles the seller payable balance to the platform ledger, with Controller review of the reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Commercial staff who negotiate seller terms do not calculate settlements.
Test of design: Inspect the settlement calculation logic and reconciliation template.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, recompute settlements to contract and agree the payable to the ledger.
Population / evidence source: Monthly seller settlement runs and reconciliations

Risk: Trade promotion accruals are understated and customer deductions are settled without validation, overstating net revenue.
Control objective: Ensure trade spend is accrued when the promotion is run and deductions are validated before settlement.
Control description: Monthly, the Trade Finance Manager accrues promotional spend from approved promotion plans and shipment volumes, and customer deductions are matched to an approved promotion before clearing; unmatched deductions above threshold are disputed and escalated.
Segregation of duties: Sales staff approving promotions do not clear the related customer deductions.
Test of design: Inspect the accrual methodology and the deduction matching and dispute workflow.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the accrual and trace a sample of cleared deductions to approved promotions.
Population / evidence source: Monthly trade accruals and deduction clearing records

Risk: Sales are pushed into the distributor channel at period end beyond genuine demand, pulling forward revenue that later reverses as returns.
Control objective: Ensure revenue reflects genuine sell-through and period-end shipment patterns are scrutinised.
Control description: Monthly, the Commercial Controller analyses shipment volumes in the final week against the period average by distributor, reviews distributor inventory and sell-through data, and material period-end spikes require documented commercial justification approved by the Chief Financial Officer.
Segregation of duties: Sales leadership whose targets are affected do not approve their own justification.
Test of design: Inspect the analysis methodology, sell-through data source and escalation criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of period ends, re-perform the shipment pattern analysis and inspect justification and approval.

Risk: A contaminated or defective batch cannot be traced and withdrawn quickly, extending consumer harm and financial exposure.
Control objective: Ensure batch traceability is maintained end to end and recall capability is tested.
Control description: Batch codes are captured at production, warehousing and despatch, and the Quality Director performs a documented mock recall at least annually, tracing a batch forward to customers and back to raw materials within the target time, with gaps remediated.
Segregation of duties: The mock recall is assessed by quality assurance independently of the operations team executing it.
Test of design: Inspect the traceability design and the mock recall procedure and target times.
Test of operating effectiveness: Obtain the most recent mock recall report; re-perform the trace for one batch and test remediation of identified gaps.

Risk: Finished goods approaching expiry are not provided for or withdrawn, overstating inventory and risking sale of out-of-date product.
Control objective: Ensure short-dated and expired stock is identified, provided for and withdrawn from sale.
Control description: Weekly, the Supply Chain Planner reviews the stock ageing and shelf-life report, blocks stock inside the minimum remaining-life window from despatch in the system, and Finance provides for short-dated stock monthly with Controller approval.
Segregation of duties: Planners blocking stock do not approve the resulting provision.
Test of design: Inspect the shelf-life blocking configuration and the provisioning policy.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of periods, test that blocked stock was not despatched and re-perform the provision.
Population / evidence source: Weekly shelf-life reports and monthly provisions

Risk: Consumption is estimated rather than metered and the unbilled revenue accrual is unsupported, misstating revenue.
Control objective: Ensure billed consumption reflects metered usage and unbilled revenue is supportable.
Control description: Monthly, the Revenue Assurance Manager reconciles energy delivered into the network to energy billed plus estimated unbilled plus technical losses, and reviews the proportion of accounts on estimated reads with the Controller approving the unbilled accrual.
Segregation of duties: Metering operations staff do not prepare or approve the revenue accrual.
Test of design: Inspect the energy balance methodology and the unbilled accrual basis.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the energy balance and recompute the unbilled accrual.
Population / evidence source: Monthly energy balances and unbilled accruals

Risk: Tariffs are applied outside the regulator-approved schedule, or regulatory returns misstate performance, triggering penalties and rebates.
Control objective: Ensure customer tariffs and regulatory submissions comply with the approved determination.
Control description: Tariff changes are configured only from the regulator-approved schedule with independent verification of the configuration before activation, and the Regulatory Affairs Manager reviews each periodic return against source data before submission.
Segregation of duties: The person configuring the tariff table does not verify or activate it.
Test of design: Inspect the tariff change procedure and the return review protocol.
Test of operating effectiveness: For all tariff changes in the period, agree configuration to the approved schedule and inspect independent verification.
Population / evidence source: Tariff change records and regulatory submissions

Risk: Network capital projects are capitalised before assets are commissioned, or overhead is over-absorbed into capital, overstating the asset base.
Control objective: Ensure network assets are capitalised only when available for use and at supportable cost.
Control description: Monthly, the Fixed Asset Manager reviews work in progress ageing and evidence of commissioning before transferring projects to fixed assets, and the overhead absorption rate applied to capital is approved annually by the Controller.
Segregation of duties: Project engineers confirming commissioning are independent of the capitalisation posting.
Test of design: Inspect the capitalisation policy, WIP ageing review and overhead rate approval.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of transfers, agree to commissioning evidence and recompute overhead absorbed.
Population / evidence source: Monthly WIP reviews and capitalisation transfers

Risk: Energy trading positions breach approved risk limits, or trades are mispriced against the market curve.
Control objective: Ensure trading operates within approved limits and positions are independently valued.
Control description: Daily, the independent Risk Control function revalues open positions against an externally sourced forward curve, reports exposures against board-approved limits, and breaches are escalated same day to the Chief Risk Officer.
Segregation of duties: Risk Control is organisationally independent of the trading desk it monitors.
Test of design: Inspect the limit framework, curve sourcing and escalation protocol.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of days, re-perform the revaluation and inspect breach escalation evidence.

Risk: Usage records are lost or mis-rated between the network and billing, so services delivered are never billed.
Control objective: Ensure usage captured by the network is completely and accurately rated and billed.
Control description: Daily, the Revenue Assurance team reconciles call and data records from network elements through mediation to the billing system, investigating record loss above tolerance, and reports leakage monthly to the Chief Financial Officer.
Segregation of duties: Revenue Assurance is independent of network operations and billing.
Test of design: Inspect the end-to-end reconciliation design, tolerance levels and escalation route.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of days, re-perform the record count reconciliation and inspect investigation of variances.

Risk: Amounts due from other operators for interconnect and roaming traffic are understated or not disputed within the settlement window.
Control objective: Ensure interconnect and roaming balances are complete, agreed and settled on time.
Control description: Monthly, the Interconnect Manager reconciles outgoing and incoming traffic to partner operator statements, raises disputes within the contractual window, and the Controller reviews the ageing of unresolved disputes and related provisions.
Segregation of duties: The person raising disputes does not approve write-offs of disputed balances.
Test of design: Inspect the settlement reconciliation process and dispute window monitoring.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, agree balances to partner statements and inspect dispute records and provisions.

Risk: Services are activated for subscribers who fail credit vetting, or remain active long after non-payment, inflating receivables and bad debt.
Control objective: Ensure activation follows credit policy and non-paying subscribers are suspended on schedule.
Control description: The provisioning system enforces a credit decision before activation, and the dunning process automatically restricts and then suspends services at the policy-defined ageing points; manual overrides require Credit Manager approval and are reported monthly.
Segregation of duties: Sales staff cannot override a credit decision or delay suspension.
Test of design: Inspect the credit workflow configuration and dunning rule set.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of activations and overrides; agree to credit decisions and approvals; test suspension timing against policy.
Population / evidence source: Activations and dunning overrides in the period

Risk: Network equipment that is decommissioned or superseded by technology change remains on the balance sheet, overstating assets.
Control objective: Ensure network assets reflect equipment actually deployed and in service.
Control description: Annually, Network Engineering performs a physical verification of deployed network elements against the fixed asset register, and assets identified as decommissioned or obsolete are retired or impaired with Controller approval.
Segregation of duties: Engineering verifies existence; Finance independently posts retirements and impairments.
Test of design: Inspect the verification programme and retirement approval process.
Test of operating effectiveness: Obtain the most recent verification; test exceptions through to retirement or impairment postings.

Risk: Unauthorised changes to employee master data — salary, bank details, status — result in incorrect or fraudulent payments.
Control objective: Ensure changes to employee master data are authorised and independently verified before they affect pay.
Control description: All changes to salary, bank details and employment status are entered by HR Operations from an authorised change form and independently verified against source documentation by a second HR officer before the next payroll run; a system-generated change report is reviewed by the HR Manager each period.
Segregation of duties: The person entering the master data change cannot verify or approve it, and neither may release the payroll payment.
Test of design: Inspect the change authorisation form, verification requirement and the period-end change report.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of master data changes; agree each to an authorised form and evidence of independent verification.
Population / evidence source: All employee master data changes in the period

Risk: Bonus and incentive accruals are not supported by approved plans or actual performance outcomes, misstating employment costs.
Control objective: Ensure incentive accruals reflect approved plan terms and the current performance outcome.
Control description: Quarterly, the Reward Manager calculates the incentive accrual from approved plan rules and the latest performance forecast, and the Financial Controller reviews the calculation against plan documentation and prior-period trends before posting.
Segregation of duties: The preparer of the accrual is not a participant in the plan being accrued.
Test of design: Inspect the accrual methodology, plan documentation and evidence of Controller review.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, re-perform the accrual from plan rules and performance data.

Risk: Severance and termination payments are made outside policy or delegated authority, or leavers continue to be paid after their exit date.
Control objective: Ensure termination payments are authorised, calculated correctly, and that pay ceases on the exit date.
Control description: Termination payments are calculated by HR from the employment contract and policy, approved at the authority level set by value, and a leaver exception report comparing termination dates to the payroll master is reviewed by the HR Manager before each payroll run.
Segregation of duties: The manager initiating the termination does not approve the settlement amount alone.
Test of design: Inspect the severance authority matrix and the leaver exception report design.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of terminations; recompute the settlement, agree the approval, and test that pay ceased on the exit date.

Risk: Freight revenue is recognised on despatch rather than over the transit period, overstating revenue at period end for shipments still in transit.
Control objective: Ensure freight revenue is recognised as the performance obligation is satisfied, with in-transit shipments deferred.
Control description: At each month end the Revenue Accounting Manager calculates the in-transit revenue deferral using the delivered-versus-despatched shipment report and average transit days by lane, and reviews the calculation against the prior month and volume trends before posting.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the deferral calculation is independent of operations reporting shipment status.
Test of design: Inspect the deferral methodology and confirm it reflects the transit-period recognition policy under IFRS 15 / ASC 606.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, re-perform the deferral using the underlying shipment report and agree the journal entry posted.
Population / evidence source: Monthly in-transit deferral calculations and supporting shipment reports

Risk: Fuel surcharge is billed at a rate inconsistent with the published index or the contractual cap, misstating revenue.
Control objective: Ensure the fuel surcharge applied in billing agrees to the published index and contractual terms.
Control description: Weekly, the Pricing Analyst updates the fuel surcharge table from the published index and a second analyst independently agrees the uploaded rate to the index source before the table is activated in the rate engine.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the rate upload cannot approve activation of the rate table.
Test of design: Inspect the surcharge procedure and rate engine configuration confirming dual sign-off before activation.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of weeks; agree the activated surcharge rate to the published index and inspect independent review evidence.

Risk: Delivered shipments remain unbilled at period end and unbilled revenue is not accrued, understating revenue and receivables.
Control objective: Ensure all delivered but uninvoiced shipments are identified and accrued at period end.
Control description: At month end the Billing Manager reviews the aged unbilled shipment report, investigates items ageing beyond five days, and the Controller reviews and approves the resulting unbilled revenue accrual.
Segregation of duties: Billing staff resolving unbilled items do not approve the accrual.
Test of design: Inspect the unbilled reporting process and evidence of Controller review and approval.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of months, agree the accrual to the aged unbilled report and inspect investigation of aged items.
Population / evidence source: Monthly unbilled shipment reports and accrual journals

Risk: Purchased transportation costs for moves completed but not yet invoiced by carriers are omitted, understating cost of sales.
Control objective: Ensure accrued purchased transportation is complete and based on contracted rates.
Control description: At month end the Transportation Controller accrues purchased transportation for completed loads without carrier invoices, valued at the rate confirmation, and reviews the accrual against subsequent invoicing in the following month (lookback analysis).
Segregation of duties: Operations staff confirming load completion are independent of the accrual preparer.
Test of design: Inspect the accrual methodology and the lookback analysis comparing prior accruals to actual invoices.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform the accrual for a sample of months from the completed-load report and rate confirmations; review lookback variances.
Population / evidence source: Monthly purchased transportation accruals and lookback analyses

Risk: The provision for cargo loss and damage claims is understated because reported incidents are not fully captured or are valued below expected settlement.
Control objective: Ensure the cargo claims provision reflects all reported incidents at an appropriate estimate of settlement value.
Control description: Quarterly, the Claims Manager reconciles the claims register to the OS&D incident log and to the general ledger provision, and the Controller reviews the actuarial or historical settlement-ratio assumption applied to open claims.
Segregation of duties: Claims handlers who set individual reserves do not approve the aggregate provision assumption.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and evidence of Controller review of the settlement assumption.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of quarters, re-perform the reconciliation and recompute the provision using the approved settlement ratio.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly claims reconciliations and provision calculations

Risk: Vehicle useful lives and residual values are not revised for changes in fleet strategy or used-vehicle markets, misstating depreciation.
Control objective: Ensure fleet useful lives and residual values remain supportable and are reviewed at least annually.
Control description: Annually the Fixed Asset Manager compares realised disposal proceeds against carried residual values by vehicle class and presents proposed revisions to the Controller for approval before the depreciation run is updated.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the residual analysis does not approve the change to master data.
Test of design: Inspect the annual review procedure and evidence of Controller approval of assumption changes.
Test of operating effectiveness: Obtain the most recent review; recompute the proceeds-to-residual comparison and agree approved changes to the asset master.

Risk: Fictitious or unauthorised vendors are created in the vendor master, enabling payments for goods or services never received.
Control objective: Ensure all vendor master additions and changes are validated and authorised before activation.
Control description: All new vendors and changes to existing vendor bank details are independently verified against supporting documentation and approved by the Vendor Master Supervisor before the record is activated in the ERP.
Segregation of duties: Requestor of a vendor change must not be the approver; neither may process payments.
Test of design: Inspect the vendor maintenance procedure and ERP workflow configuration to confirm approval is required before activation.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of vendor additions and bank detail changes; inspect evidence of independent verification and approval prior to activation.
Population / evidence source: ERP vendor master change log for the period

Risk: Dormant, duplicate or superseded vendor records remain active and are used to route improper payments.
Control objective: Ensure the vendor master remains accurate and free of duplicate or dormant records.
Control description: The AP Manager performs a quarterly review of the vendor master for duplicates, dormant vendors and incomplete records, and initiates deactivation where required. Review is evidenced and retained.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer must be independent of vendor master maintenance.
Test of design: Inspect the review template and confirm it addresses duplicates, dormancy and completeness.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each quarter in the period, inspect the completed review, exceptions identified, and evidence of follow-up action.

Risk: A single individual can create a vendor and release a payment to it, allowing undetected misappropriation.
Control objective: Ensure incompatible duties within the purchasing and payment cycle are segregated in the ERP.
Control description: ERP role configuration prevents any single user from holding both vendor master maintenance and payment release entitlements. Conflicts are blocked at role assignment.
Segregation of duties: This control is itself the segregation mechanism; changes to the SoD ruleset require independent approval.
Test of design: Inspect the SoD ruleset configuration and confirm the conflict pair is defined and set to block rather than warn.
Test of operating effectiveness: Attempt assignment of a conflicting role in a test client, or inspect system evidence that conflicting assignments were rejected during the period. Inspect any approved mitigating-control exceptions.
Population / evidence source: ERP role conflict report and access change log

Risk: Goods or services are committed without authorisation, resulting in unapproved expenditure.
Control objective: Ensure all purchase requisitions are approved in accordance with the delegation of authority.
Control description: The ERP workflow routes every purchase requisition for electronic approval according to the delegation of authority matrix based on value and cost centre. Requisitions cannot convert to a purchase order without approval.
Segregation of duties: Requestor cannot self-approve; workflow enforces a different approver.
Test of design: Inspect the delegation of authority matrix and reconcile approval thresholds configured in the workflow to it.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of requisitions across value bands; inspect system approval history for approval by an authorised approver prior to PO creation. Test the configuration for a low and high value band.
Population / evidence source: ERP requisition table for the period

Risk: Purchase orders are issued without an approved requisition, bypassing the authorisation process.
Control objective: Ensure purchase orders originate only from approved requisitions.
Control description: The ERP prevents creation of a purchase order that is not linked to an approved requisition. Free-text POs are disabled for all users other than an approved emergency-purchase role.
Segregation of duties: Emergency-purchase role holders must not approve their own POs.
Test of design: Inspect ERP configuration confirming the requisition-to-PO link is mandatory.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect a system-generated listing of POs without a linked requisition for the period and evaluate each. Re-perform by attempting PO creation without a requisition.

Risk: Invoices are paid for goods or services not ordered or not received, or at incorrect prices or quantities.
Control objective: Ensure invoices are matched to an approved purchase order and evidence of receipt before payment.
Control description: The ERP performs an automated three-way match of purchase order, goods receipt and supplier invoice. Invoices failing the match are blocked from payment and routed to an exception queue.
Segregation of duties: AP processors cannot override a match block; override requires AP Manager entitlement.
Test of design: Inspect the match configuration, including which document types are subject to match and the block behaviour on failure.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform the match on a sample of invoices. Inspect the exception queue for the period to confirm blocked invoices were not released without resolution.
Population / evidence source: ERP invoice register and match exception log

Risk: Match tolerances are set too wide or exceptions are cleared without investigation, allowing overpayment.
Control objective: Ensure match exceptions and tolerance settings are reviewed and resolved appropriately.
Control description: Match tolerance parameters are configured centrally and changes require approval. The AP Manager reviews and clears the match exception report weekly, evidencing investigation and resolution of each item.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer must be independent of invoice entry.
Test of design: Inspect the tolerance configuration and the change-approval process. Inspect the exception review template.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of weekly reviews; inspect evidence of investigation and resolution. Inspect all tolerance parameter changes in the period for approval.
Population / evidence source: Weekly match exception reports; tolerance change log

Risk: Goods or services received are not recorded, understating liabilities and expenses in the correct period.
Control objective: Ensure receipts are recorded completely and in the period in which they occur.
Control description: Warehouse personnel record goods receipt in the ERP against the purchase order at the point of delivery. The ERP records the receipt date independently of the user-entered date.
Segregation of duties: Receiving function segregated from purchasing and from invoice approval.
Test of design: Inspect the receiving procedure and confirm system date capture is independent of user entry.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of deliveries from carrier documentation and trace to timely recording in the ERP. Test period-end cutoff either side of the reporting date.
Population / evidence source: Goods receipt table; carrier delivery documentation
Sample size guidance: 25, plus cutoff testing at period end

Risk: Duplicate invoices are entered and paid twice, overstating expenses and cash outflows.
Control objective: Ensure duplicate invoices are prevented from being recorded.
Control description: The ERP blocks entry of an invoice where vendor, invoice number, date and amount match an existing document. Blocked entries are logged and require AP Manager review to release.
Segregation of duties: Releasing a duplicate block requires an entitlement not held by invoice processors.
Test of design: Inspect the duplicate check configuration, including which fields form the match key.
Test of operating effectiveness: Attempt entry of a known duplicate in a test client. Inspect the log of blocked and released duplicates for the period and evaluate each release.

Risk: Invoices without a purchase order are approved by individuals without appropriate authority.
Control objective: Ensure non-PO invoices are approved in line with the delegation of authority.
Control description: Non-PO invoices are routed through the ERP workflow for approval by cost centre owner and, above threshold, by a second approver, in accordance with the delegation of authority matrix.
Segregation of duties: Approver cannot be the invoice requestor or the payment releaser.
Test of design: Reconcile workflow approval thresholds to the delegation of authority matrix.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of non-PO invoices across value bands; inspect approval history for approval by an authorised approver prior to payment.

Risk: Goods received but not invoiced at period end are not accrued, understating liabilities.
Control objective: Ensure the goods received not invoiced accrual is complete and accurate at each period end.
Control description: At each month end the Financial Accountant prepares the GR/IR accrual from the system-generated aged goods-received-not-invoiced report, investigates aged items, and the Financial Controller reviews and approves the accrual and supporting reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer must be different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the accrual methodology and the aged GR/IR report definition.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; re-perform the accrual calculation from the underlying report and inspect evidence of review and approval, including investigation of aged items.
Population / evidence source: Monthly GR/IR reports and accrual workpapers

Risk: The accounts payable subledger does not agree to the general ledger, indicating unrecorded or erroneous transactions.
Control objective: Ensure the AP subledger reconciles to the general ledger each period.
Control description: The Financial Accountant reconciles the AP subledger to the general ledger control account monthly. Reconciling items are identified, explained and cleared. The Financial Controller reviews and approves the reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Preparer independent of reviewer; neither posts manual journals to the AP control account.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the threshold for investigating reconciling items.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of monthly reconciliations; verify mathematical accuracy, agreement to source reports, ageing and clearance of reconciling items, and evidence of timely review.

Risk: Payments are released for invoices that are unapproved, altered or fraudulent.
Control objective: Ensure payment runs are reviewed and authorised before release to the bank.
Control description: Prior to release, the Treasury Manager reviews the payment proposal against supporting approved invoices and authorises the run. Release to the bank requires dual authorisation by two nominated signatories.
Segregation of duties: Payment releasers must not maintain vendor master data or process invoices.
Test of design: Inspect the payment authorisation procedure and bank mandate confirming dual authorisation limits.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of payment runs; inspect evidence of review against supporting invoices and dual authorisation prior to transmission.
Population / evidence source: Payment run listings and bank authorisation records

Risk: The payment file is altered between approval in the ERP and receipt by the bank.
Control objective: Ensure the integrity of the payment file in transit to the bank.
Control description: Payment files are transmitted to the bank over an encrypted channel with hash-total validation. The bank rejects files failing validation, and rejections are investigated by Treasury.
Segregation of duties: File transmission access restricted and segregated from payment approval.
Test of design: Inspect the interface configuration, encryption and hash-total validation settings.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the transmission log for the period for rejected or failed files and evidence of investigation. Confirm control totals agree between ERP and bank confirmations for a sample.

Risk: Debit balances and long-outstanding items in accounts payable indicate unrecovered overpayments or misstatement.
Control objective: Ensure aged and debit balances in accounts payable are identified and resolved.
Control description: The AP Manager reviews the aged accounts payable listing monthly, investigating debit balances and items outstanding beyond terms, and documents resolution.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer independent of invoice processing.
Test of design: Inspect the review procedure and the ageing report parameters.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of monthly reviews; inspect evidence of investigation and resolution of debit and aged balances.

Risk: Fictitious or unauthorised customers are created, or remittance details are altered, enabling diversion of receipts or recognition of invalid revenue.
Control objective: Ensure customer master additions and changes are verified and authorised before activation.
Control description: New customers and changes to existing customer bank or remittance details are independently verified against supporting documentation and approved by the Credit Manager before the record is activated in the ERP.
Segregation of duties: Requestor of a customer change must not approve it, and must not apply cash receipts.
Test of design: Inspect the customer maintenance procedure and ERP workflow to confirm approval precedes activation.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of customer additions and remittance detail changes; inspect evidence of verification and approval prior to activation.

Risk: Credit is extended to customers without assessment of creditworthiness, resulting in receivables that are not collectable.
Control objective: Ensure customer credit limits are assessed and approved in line with the credit policy.
Control description: Credit limits are established from a documented credit assessment and approved in accordance with the credit policy authority matrix. Limits are reassessed at least annually and on trigger events.
Segregation of duties: Credit assessment prepared and approved by different individuals; approver independent of sales.
Test of design: Inspect the credit policy and reconcile approval thresholds to the authority matrix.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of new and revised credit limits; inspect the credit assessment and approval at the appropriate authority level.

Risk: Orders are released to customers who are over their credit limit or on hold, increasing exposure to uncollectable balances.
Control objective: Ensure orders exceeding credit limits are blocked and released only with authorisation.
Control description: The ERP automatically places on hold any sales order that would take the customer beyond the approved credit limit or that is past due. Release requires Credit Manager entitlement and is logged.
Segregation of duties: Sales personnel do not hold credit release entitlement.
Test of design: Inspect the credit check configuration and confirm the hold is enforced rather than advisory.
Test of operating effectiveness: Attempt order entry beyond limit in a test client. Inspect the credit release log for the period and evaluate releases for authorisation.
Population / evidence source: ERP credit hold and release log

Risk: Sales are invoiced at incorrect prices or unauthorised discounts, misstating revenue and receivables.
Control objective: Ensure prices and discounts applied to sales orders are authorised and accurate.
Control description: Price and discount master data changes require approval by the Commercial Director in line with the pricing policy. The ERP defaults pricing from the approved master; manual overrides are blocked above defined discount thresholds.
Segregation of duties: Sales representatives cannot amend the price master or approve their own discount overrides.
Test of design: Inspect the pricing policy, the price master change workflow, and the override threshold configuration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of price master changes and of discount overrides; inspect approval. Re-perform pricing on a sample of invoices against the approved price master.
Population / evidence source: Price master change log; invoice register

Risk: Goods are despatched without a valid sales order, or despatches are not recorded, leading to unbilled shipments and understated revenue.
Control objective: Ensure all despatches are supported by an approved order and are recorded completely.
Control description: Goods are released from the warehouse only against an approved sales order. Despatch is recorded in the ERP at the point of shipment and generates a shipping document referenced to the order.
Segregation of duties: Warehouse despatch segregated from order entry and from invoicing.
Test of design: Inspect the despatch procedure and ERP configuration linking despatch to an approved order.
Test of operating effectiveness: Trace a sample of shipping documents to approved orders and to recording in the ERP. Test cutoff either side of period end.
Population / evidence source: Shipping document file; ERP delivery table

Risk: Shipments are not invoiced, or are invoiced more than once, misstating revenue and receivables.
Control objective: Ensure all despatches are invoiced once, completely and accurately.
Control description: The ERP generates invoices from despatch records. The Billing Supervisor reviews the daily exception report of despatches not invoiced and invoices without a despatch, and resolves all items.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer independent of despatch recording.
Test of design: Inspect the exception report definition and confirm it captures both directions of mismatch.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of daily reviews; inspect evidence of investigation and clearance of exceptions.

Risk: Revenue is recognised in the incorrect period or before the performance obligation is satisfied, misstating reported results.
Control objective: Ensure revenue is recognised in accordance with the applicable framework and in the correct period.
Control description: The Financial Controller reviews the revenue recognition analysis at each period end, confirming that performance obligations, transfer of control and contract terms support the timing and amount recognised, including for non-standard and multi-element arrangements.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the analysis is not the reviewer; commercial teams do not determine accounting conclusions.
Test of design: Inspect the revenue recognition policy and the review template, including criteria for identifying non-standard arrangements.
