Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; re-perform the analysis for a selection of contracts and inspect evidence of review and conclusion.
Population / evidence source: Monthly revenue recognition files; contract register

Risk: Credit notes are issued without justification to conceal uncollectable balances or fictitious sales.
Control objective: Ensure credit notes are supported and authorised in line with the delegation of authority.
Control description: Credit notes require documented justification and approval per the delegation of authority. Credits above threshold require Financial Controller approval. The ERP blocks posting without approval.
Segregation of duties: Raiser of a credit note cannot approve it; sales cannot approve credits to their own accounts.
Test of design: Reconcile credit note approval thresholds to the delegation of authority.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of credit notes across value bands; inspect supporting justification and approval prior to posting.

Risk: Receipts are misapplied or misappropriated, and customer balances are misstated.
Control objective: Ensure customer receipts are applied accurately and completely to the correct accounts.
Control description: Receipts are applied from the bank statement to customer accounts daily. Unapplied and suspense items are reviewed weekly by the AR Supervisor and cleared. Application is reconciled to bank receipts.
Segregation of duties: Cash application segregated from credit note approval, customer master and bank reconciliation.
Test of design: Inspect the cash application procedure and the unapplied cash review template.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of weekly reviews; inspect ageing and clearance of unapplied items. Reconcile receipts applied to bank receipts for a sample of days.

Risk: The accounts receivable subledger does not agree to the general ledger, indicating unrecorded or erroneous transactions.
Control objective: Ensure the AR subledger reconciles to the general ledger each period.
Control description: The Financial Accountant reconciles the AR subledger to the general ledger control account monthly. Reconciling items are explained and cleared, and the reconciliation is reviewed and approved by the Financial Controller.
Segregation of duties: Preparer independent of reviewer; neither posts manual journals to the AR control account.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the investigation threshold for reconciling items.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of monthly reconciliations; verify accuracy, agreement to source reports, and evidence of timely review.

Risk: The allowance for expected credit losses is understated, overstating receivables and results.
Control objective: Ensure the allowance for expected credit losses is complete and supportable.
Control description: The Credit Manager prepares the expected credit loss calculation quarterly using the approved provisioning matrix and specific assessment of significant or disputed balances. The Financial Controller reviews and approves the provision and the underlying assumptions.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer are different; sales does not influence provisioning conclusions.
Test of design: Inspect the provisioning methodology, the ageing bands and the loss rates applied.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select the quarters in the period; re-perform the calculation and inspect support for specific provisions and for changes in assumptions.
Population / evidence source: Quarterly ECL calculations and AR ageing

Risk: A single individual can create a customer, raise a credit note and apply cash, enabling concealment of misappropriated receipts.
Control objective: Ensure incompatible duties across the order to cash cycle are segregated in the ERP.
Control description: ERP role configuration prevents any single user from holding customer master maintenance, credit note approval and cash application entitlements. Conflicts are blocked at role assignment.
Segregation of duties: This control is the segregation mechanism; ruleset changes require independent approval.
Test of design: Inspect the SoD ruleset and confirm the conflict set is defined and blocking.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the role conflict report for the period, plus any approved mitigating-control exceptions.

Risk: Standard costs are inaccurate or updated without authorisation, misstating inventory valuation and cost of sales.
Control objective: Ensure standard cost changes are supported and authorised before release.
Control description: Proposed standard cost changes are supported by current input costs and bills of material, reviewed by the Cost Accountant and approved by the Financial Controller before the cost roll is released.
Segregation of duties: Cost preparer does not release the cost roll to production.
Test of design: Inspect the costing policy and the cost roll release procedure.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each cost roll in the period, inspect the supporting analysis and evidence of approval prior to release.

Risk: Cost variances are not investigated, so errors in costing or consumption remain in inventory and cost of sales.
Control objective: Ensure manufacturing and purchase price variances are analysed and resolved.
Control description: The Cost Accountant prepares a monthly analysis of purchase price, usage and labour variances against threshold, investigates items exceeding tolerance, and the Financial Controller reviews the analysis and the resulting adjustments.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the variance report definition and the investigation thresholds.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; inspect the analysis, evidence of investigation of items above tolerance, and review approval.

Risk: Recorded inventory quantities do not reflect quantities on hand, misstating inventory and cost of sales.
Control objective: Ensure recorded inventory quantities are validated by physical count.
Control description: A cycle count programme covers all stock locations over the year, with high-value items counted more frequently. Counts are performed by personnel independent of custody, and results are reconciled to system quantities.
Segregation of duties: Counters independent of warehouse custody; count sheets not pre-populated with system quantities.
Test of design: Inspect the cycle count programme and confirm coverage of all locations and frequency by value band.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of counts; inspect count sheets, reconciliation to system quantities and investigation of differences. Observe a count where possible.

Risk: Count differences are adjusted into the ledger without investigation or authorisation, concealing loss or theft.
Control objective: Ensure inventory adjustments arising from counts are investigated and authorised.
Control description: Count differences above threshold are investigated and documented. All inventory adjustments require approval by the Operations Director, and adjustments above a higher threshold require Financial Controller approval.
Segregation of duties: Warehouse personnel cannot approve adjustments to inventory they hold custody of.
Test of design: Reconcile adjustment approval thresholds to the delegation of authority.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of inventory adjustments; inspect investigation documentation and approval at the appropriate level.

Risk: Slow-moving, obsolete or damaged inventory is not provided against, overstating inventory.
Control objective: Ensure the inventory provision reflects slow-moving and obsolete stock.
Control description: The Cost Accountant prepares the excess and obsolete provision quarterly using the approved ageing and usage-based matrix, supplemented by specific assessment from Operations. The Financial Controller reviews and approves the provision.
Segregation of duties: Operations input is documented but does not override the policy matrix without approval.
Test of design: Inspect the provisioning policy, ageing bands and provision percentages.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each quarter, re-perform the calculation and inspect support for specific provisions and for any deviation from the matrix.

Risk: Inventory is carried above net realisable value, overstating assets.
Control objective: Ensure inventory is stated at the lower of cost and net realisable value.
Control description: At each period end the Cost Accountant compares carrying cost to expected selling price less costs to sell for significant inventory categories, and records a write-down where required. The Financial Controller reviews the assessment.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the NRV assessment methodology and the basis for expected selling prices.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of categories, re-perform the NRV comparison and inspect evidence of review.

Risk: Inventory movements around period end are recorded in the wrong period, misstating inventory and cost of sales.
Control objective: Ensure inventory receipts, despatches and transfers are recorded in the correct period.
Control description: At each period end the Inventory Control Manager reviews goods received and despatched in the days either side of the cutoff date against supporting documentation to confirm recording in the correct period, including goods in transit.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer independent of warehouse recording.
Test of design: Inspect the cutoff review procedure and the number of days either side reviewed.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of period ends; inspect the cutoff testing performed and any corrections made.

Risk: The inventory subledger does not agree to the general ledger, indicating unrecorded movements or valuation errors.
Control objective: Ensure the inventory subledger reconciles to the general ledger each period.
Control description: The Cost Accountant reconciles the inventory subledger to the general ledger monthly, explains and clears reconciling items, and the Financial Controller reviews and approves the reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Preparer independent of reviewer.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the threshold for investigating items.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of monthly reconciliations; verify accuracy and evidence of timely review.

Risk: Inventory held by or for third parties is omitted or double counted, misstating inventory and rights to it.
Control objective: Ensure consignment and third-party held inventory is accounted for correctly.
Control description: The Inventory Control Manager maintains a register of inventory held at third-party locations and inventory held on consignment for others, agreed quarterly to third-party statements or confirmations.
Segregation of duties: Register maintained independently of the warehouse holding the stock.
Test of design: Inspect the register and the confirmation process with third parties.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each quarter, inspect the agreement of the register to third-party confirmations and resolution of differences.

Risk: Fictitious employees are added to payroll, or pay rates and bank details are altered without authorisation.
Control objective: Ensure employee master additions and changes are authorised and supported.
Control description: New hires and changes to pay rate or bank details are entered from an approved HR instruction and independently verified against the personnel file before the next payroll run. Changes are evidenced on the payroll change report.
Segregation of duties: Payroll processors cannot amend employee master data; HR cannot process payment runs.
Test of design: Inspect the starter and change procedure and the interface between HR and payroll systems.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of new hires and pay rate and bank detail changes; inspect the approved instruction and evidence of verification.

Risk: Leavers remain on payroll after termination, resulting in payments to individuals no longer employed.
Control objective: Ensure terminations are processed on payroll promptly and completely.
Control description: HR notifies payroll of all terminations through the workflow. The Payroll Manager reconciles the leaver report to payroll deletions each cycle and investigates any employee paid after their termination date.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer independent of employee master maintenance.
Test of design: Inspect the termination workflow and the leaver reconciliation template.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of payroll cycles; reconcile the HR leaver report to payroll deletions and inspect investigation of any post-termination payments.

Risk: Employees are paid for hours not worked, or overtime is claimed without authorisation.
Control objective: Ensure hours and overtime are approved before being paid.
Control description: Timesheets and overtime are approved electronically by the employee's line manager before transfer to payroll. Unapproved time is not paid and is reported as an exception.
Segregation of duties: Employees cannot approve their own time; approver must be the designated line manager.
Test of design: Inspect the time system configuration confirming approval is required before transfer to payroll.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of pay periods; inspect the approval status of time transferred and the exception report of unapproved time.

Risk: Errors or unauthorised amendments in the payroll run result in incorrect payments and misstated payroll expense.
Control objective: Ensure the payroll run is reviewed and authorised before disbursement.
Control description: Before disbursement the Payroll Manager reviews the payroll register against the prior period, investigating variances above threshold and all exception items. The Financial Controller approves the total payroll for release.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the payroll run does not approve it or release payment.
Test of design: Inspect the review template, the variance threshold and the approval requirement before release.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of payroll runs; inspect the variance analysis, investigation of exceptions and approval prior to disbursement.
Population / evidence source: Monthly payroll registers and review files

Risk: The payroll payment file is altered or released without authorisation, enabling diversion of funds.
Control objective: Ensure payroll disbursements are authorised and transmitted intact.
Control description: The payroll payment file is released to the bank under dual authorisation by nominated signatories, with control totals agreed to the approved payroll register before transmission.
Segregation of duties: Payroll processors do not hold bank release entitlements.
Test of design: Inspect the bank mandate and the dual authorisation configuration for payroll files.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of payroll disbursements; inspect agreement of control totals to the approved register and evidence of dual authorisation.
Population / evidence source: Payroll payment files and bank authorisations

Risk: Manual or off-cycle payments are made outside the normal controls, concealing unauthorised payments.
Control objective: Ensure off-cycle and manual payroll payments are justified and approved.
Control description: All off-cycle payments require documented justification and approval by the HR Director and Financial Controller before processing, and are reported in the monthly payroll review.
Segregation of duties: Requestor cannot approve; two approvers required.
Test of design: Inspect the off-cycle payment procedure and approval requirements.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the full population of off-cycle payments for the period for justification and dual approval.

Risk: Statutory deductions are calculated incorrectly or remitted late, resulting in liabilities, interest and penalties.
Control objective: Ensure statutory deductions are accurate and remitted by the due date.
Control description: The Payroll Manager reconciles statutory deductions per the payroll register to amounts remitted each period and confirms remittance by the statutory deadline. Differences are investigated and cleared.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the remittance is not the sole reviewer of the reconciliation.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the calendar of statutory deadlines.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of periods; re-perform the reconciliation and inspect evidence of timely remittance.

Risk: Bonus and incentive payments are calculated incorrectly or paid without authorisation, misstating payroll expense.
Control objective: Ensure incentive payments are calculated in accordance with approved schemes and authorised.
Control description: Incentive calculations are prepared from the approved scheme rules and achieved performance data, independently reviewed for accuracy, and approved by the HR Director. Executive incentives are approved by the Remuneration Committee.
Segregation of duties: Recipients do not calculate or approve their own incentive; executive awards escalate to the committee.
Test of design: Inspect the scheme rules and the approval matrix, including the escalation for executive awards.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform a sample of incentive calculations against scheme rules and performance data; inspect approval at the required level.

Risk: Payroll costs and related liabilities are not completely recorded in the general ledger.
Control objective: Ensure payroll postings reconcile to the general ledger each period.
Control description: The Financial Accountant reconciles the payroll register to payroll expense and liability accounts in the general ledger monthly. Reconciling items are explained and cleared, and the Financial Controller reviews the reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Preparer independent of reviewer and of payroll processing.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the accounts covered.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of monthly reconciliations; verify accuracy and evidence of review.

Risk: A single individual can add an employee, process the payroll and release the payment, enabling payments to fictitious employees.
Control objective: Ensure incompatible payroll duties are segregated.
Control description: System access is configured so that no individual holds employee master maintenance, payroll processing and payment release entitlements. Conflicts are blocked at role assignment and reviewed periodically.
Segregation of duties: This control is the segregation mechanism; exceptions require documented mitigating controls.
Test of design: Inspect the access ruleset and confirm the conflict set is defined and blocking.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the role conflict report for the period and evaluate any exceptions and mitigating controls.
Population / evidence source: Payroll and HR system access reports

Risk: Capital expenditure is incurred without authorisation, resulting in unapproved commitments and asset additions.
Control objective: Ensure capital expenditure is authorised in line with the delegation of authority.
Control description: Capital expenditure requests are supported by a business case and approved per the capital authority matrix, with amounts above threshold requiring Board approval, before commitment is made.
Segregation of duties: Requestor cannot approve; Board approval required above threshold.
Test of design: Reconcile the capital authority matrix to the delegation of authority and to Board minutes.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of capital projects; inspect the business case and approval at the required level prior to commitment.

Risk: Costs are capitalised that should be expensed, or vice versa, misstating assets and results.
Control objective: Ensure costs are capitalised only where they meet the capitalisation policy.
Control description: The Fixed Asset Accountant assesses each addition against the capitalisation policy, including the capitalisation threshold and the treatment of directly attributable costs. The Financial Controller reviews additions above threshold.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the capitalisation policy and the review threshold.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of additions; inspect the assessment against policy and evidence of review where above threshold.

Risk: Asset disposals are not recorded, or proceeds are misappropriated, overstating assets and understating gains.
Control objective: Ensure disposals are authorised, recorded and proceeds accounted for.
Control description: Disposals require approval per the delegation of authority. The Fixed Asset Accountant removes the asset and accumulated depreciation on disposal and agrees proceeds to the bank. Disposals are reported monthly.
Segregation of duties: Custodian of the asset cannot approve its disposal or receive the proceeds.
Test of design: Inspect the disposal procedure and approval thresholds.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of disposals; inspect approval, removal from the register, and agreement of proceeds to bank.

Risk: Depreciation is calculated incorrectly or on inappropriate lives, misstating carrying value and expense.
Control objective: Ensure depreciation is calculated in accordance with policy and reviewed for reasonableness.
Control description: Depreciation is calculated automatically by the fixed asset system from the asset class, life and in-service date. The Fixed Asset Accountant reviews the monthly depreciation charge for reasonableness against expectation and investigates variances.
Segregation of duties: Asset class and life defaults cannot be amended by the preparer without approval.
Test of design: Inspect the depreciation configuration by asset class and the review template.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform depreciation for a sample of assets; inspect the monthly reasonableness review and investigation of variances.

Risk: Useful lives and residual values are not reassessed, so carrying values do not reflect the pattern of consumption.
Control objective: Ensure useful lives and residual values are reviewed at least annually.
Control description: The Fixed Asset Accountant reviews useful lives and residual values annually against usage and asset condition, and the Financial Controller approves any changes and their prospective application.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and approver are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the review procedure and the basis for assessing lives.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the annual review performed in the period, changes made and evidence of approval.

Risk: Assets recorded in the register no longer exist or are not in use, overstating assets.
Control objective: Ensure recorded assets are validated by physical verification.
Control description: A rolling programme of physical verification covers all asset locations over a defined cycle. Results are reconciled to the fixed asset register and differences are investigated and adjusted with approval.
Segregation of duties: Verifier independent of the custodian of the assets.
Test of design: Inspect the verification programme and its coverage cycle.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect verification records for the period, reconciliation to the register, and approval of adjustments.

Risk: Assets remain in construction in progress after being brought into use, deferring depreciation and overstating results.
Control objective: Ensure assets are transferred from CIP to in-service on commissioning.
Control description: The Fixed Asset Accountant reviews the CIP balance monthly, agrees each project to its status with the project manager, and transfers commissioned assets into service in the month they become available for use.
Segregation of duties: Project status confirmed by project management, not by the accountant alone.
Test of design: Inspect the CIP review procedure and the criteria for available for use.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; inspect the CIP review, project status confirmations and timeliness of transfers.

Risk: Impaired assets are not written down, overstating carrying value.
Control objective: Ensure indicators of impairment are identified and assessed.
Control description: At each reporting date the Financial Controller reviews for indicators of impairment across cash generating units, and where indicators exist a recoverable amount assessment is prepared and reviewed by the CFO.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the assessment is not the approver.
Test of design: Inspect the impairment review procedure and the indicator checklist.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the impairment reviews performed in the period, any recoverable amount calculations, and evidence of approval.

Risk: The fixed asset register does not agree to the general ledger, indicating unrecorded additions, disposals or depreciation.
Control objective: Ensure the fixed asset register reconciles to the general ledger each period.
Control description: The Fixed Asset Accountant reconciles the register to the general ledger monthly for cost, accumulated depreciation and net book value. Reconciling items are cleared and the Financial Controller reviews the reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Preparer independent of reviewer.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the balances covered.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of monthly reconciliations; verify accuracy and evidence of review.

Risk: Bank accounts are opened or closed, or signatories changed, without authorisation, enabling unauthorised movement of funds.
Control objective: Ensure bank account and mandate changes are authorised at the required level.
Control description: Opening and closing of bank accounts and all changes to bank mandates and signatories require approval by the CFO and, where required by the delegation of authority, by the Board. Changes are confirmed directly with the bank.
Segregation of duties: Requestor cannot approve; confirmation obtained independently from the bank.
Test of design: Inspect the treasury policy and reconcile mandate authority to the delegation of authority and Board minutes.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the full population of account and mandate changes in the period for approval and bank confirmation.

Risk: Differences between bank records and the ledger are not identified, concealing unrecorded or fraudulent transactions.
Control objective: Ensure all bank accounts are reconciled and differences resolved promptly.
Control description: All bank accounts are reconciled monthly by the Treasury Accountant to the bank statement. Reconciling items are aged, explained and cleared, and items above threshold or over 30 days are escalated. The Financial Controller reviews and approves each reconciliation.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the reconciliation does not process payments or have bank release entitlement.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template, ageing thresholds and escalation criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of account-months; verify mathematical accuracy, agreement to bank statements obtained independently, ageing and clearance of items, and timely review.

Risk: Liquidity is misjudged, resulting in an inability to meet obligations or in unnecessary borrowing cost.
Control objective: Ensure cash forecasts are prepared and reviewed to support liquidity management.
Control description: The Treasury Manager prepares a rolling cash forecast weekly, compares actual to forecast, and reports variances and liquidity headroom to the CFO monthly.
Segregation of duties: Forecast reviewed by CFO independent of preparation.
Test of design: Inspect the forecasting methodology and the reporting cycle.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of forecasts; inspect the actual to forecast comparison and evidence of CFO review.

Risk: Borrowings are entered into without authorisation, or are recorded incorrectly, misstating liabilities and finance cost.
Control objective: Ensure borrowings are authorised and accurately recorded.
Control description: New borrowing facilities and drawdowns require approval per the delegation of authority, with facilities above threshold approved by the Board. The Treasury Accountant records the instrument and agrees terms, interest and repayment schedules to the executed agreement.
Segregation of duties: Dealer does not record or settle the transaction.
Test of design: Reconcile borrowing approval thresholds to the delegation of authority and Board minutes.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the full population of new facilities and drawdowns for approval; agree recorded terms to executed agreements.

Risk: Breach of a debt covenant is not identified, resulting in misclassification of debt and potential acceleration.
Control objective: Ensure compliance with debt covenants is monitored and reported.
Control description: The Treasury Manager calculates covenant compliance each reporting period from the approved definitions and reports the position to the CFO and Audit Committee. Forecast headroom is assessed for the next twelve months.
Segregation of duties: Calculation independently reviewed before reporting.
Test of design: Inspect the covenant definitions per the agreements and the calculation methodology.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each period, re-perform the covenant calculations and inspect reporting to the CFO and Audit Committee.

Risk: Foreign exchange exposures are unidentified or unhedged, or derivatives are transacted without authorisation.
Control objective: Ensure FX exposures are identified and hedging is transacted within approved mandates.
Control description: The Treasury Manager identifies FX exposures monthly from forecast and balance sheet positions, and transacts hedges only within the limits and instrument types permitted by the Board-approved treasury policy. All deals are confirmed independently.
Segregation of duties: Dealing, confirmation and settlement performed by different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the treasury policy limits and permitted instruments.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of deals; inspect that terms fall within policy limits and that independent confirmation was obtained.

Risk: Derivatives are misvalued or hedge accounting is applied without qualifying documentation, misstating results and equity.
Control objective: Ensure derivatives are valued correctly and hedge accounting is properly documented.
Control description: Derivative valuations are obtained from the counterparty and independently corroborated. Hedge designation documentation and effectiveness testing are prepared at inception and each reporting date and reviewed by the Financial Controller.
Segregation of duties: Valuation corroborated independently of the counterparty relationship manager.
Test of design: Inspect the hedge documentation template and the effectiveness testing methodology.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of hedges, inspect designation documentation, effectiveness testing and corroboration of valuation.

Risk: Intercompany funding is advanced without authorisation or is not recorded consistently by both parties.
Control objective: Ensure intercompany funding is authorised and agreed between entities.
Control description: Intercompany loans and funding require approval per the delegation of authority and are documented in an agreement. Balances are agreed between entities monthly and differences investigated.
Segregation of duties: Both entities confirm the balance independently.
Test of design: Inspect the intercompany policy and the balance agreement process.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of periods; inspect approval of new funding and evidence of balance agreement between entities.

Risk: A single individual can transact, confirm and settle a treasury deal, enabling unauthorised or concealed transactions.
Control objective: Ensure front, middle and back office treasury duties are segregated.
Control description: Treasury system and banking entitlements are configured so that dealing, confirmation and settlement are performed by different individuals. Access is reviewed quarterly by the CFO.
Segregation of duties: This control is the segregation mechanism; exceptions require documented mitigating controls.
Test of design: Inspect entitlement configuration across dealing, confirmation and settlement functions.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the quarterly access review and any conflicts identified, together with mitigating controls.

Risk: The current tax provision is calculated incorrectly, misstating the tax charge and liability.
Control objective: Ensure the current tax provision is accurate and supportable.
Control description: The Tax Manager prepares the current tax computation from the statutory accounts, reconciling book to taxable profit and supporting each adjustment. The CFO reviews and approves the provision, with external adviser input on significant judgements.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and approver are different; external adviser review for significant judgements.
Test of design: Inspect the tax computation methodology and the review and approval requirements.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each period, re-perform the book to tax reconciliation for significant adjustments and inspect evidence of review and approval.

Risk: Deferred tax balances are incomplete or measured at incorrect rates, misstating assets, liabilities and the tax charge.
Control objective: Ensure deferred tax is complete and measured at the enacted rate.
Control description: The Tax Manager prepares the deferred tax calculation from a full listing of temporary differences, applying enacted or substantively enacted rates, and assesses recoverability of deferred tax assets against forecast taxable profits. The CFO reviews and approves.
Segregation of duties: Recoverability assessment supported by approved forecasts, not prepared in isolation by tax.
Test of design: Inspect the deferred tax methodology, the temporary difference listing and the recoverability criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: Re-perform the calculation for significant temporary differences; inspect rate support and the recoverability assessment and its approval.

Risk: Uncertain tax positions are not identified or provided for, understating liabilities.
Control objective: Ensure uncertain tax positions are identified, measured and disclosed.
Control description: The Tax Manager maintains a register of uncertain tax positions, assessing each for probability and measurement at each reporting date with external adviser input. The CFO and Audit Committee review the register annually.
Segregation of duties: External adviser input obtained independently of the preparer's conclusion.
Test of design: Inspect the register and the assessment methodology.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the register and supporting assessments; agree significant positions to adviser correspondence and to Audit Committee reporting.

Risk: Indirect tax returns are inaccurate or filed late, resulting in assessments, interest and penalties.
Control objective: Ensure indirect tax returns are accurate and filed by the due date.
Control description: Indirect tax returns are prepared from system reports, reconciled to the general ledger and to revenue and purchase records, independently reviewed by the Tax Manager, and filed by the statutory deadline.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the return preparation procedure, the reconciliation template and the filing calendar.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of returns; re-perform the reconciliation to the ledger and inspect evidence of review and timely filing.

Risk: Intercompany transactions are not priced at arm's length or are not documented, creating exposure to adjustment and penalties.
Control objective: Ensure intercompany pricing follows the transfer pricing policy and is documented.
Control description: Intercompany transactions are priced in accordance with the Board-approved transfer pricing policy. Local file and master file documentation is prepared or refreshed annually with external adviser support and reviewed by the CFO.
Segregation of duties: Pricing set by policy, not negotiated between the transacting entities.
Test of design: Inspect the transfer pricing policy and the documentation refresh cycle.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the documentation prepared in the period and evidence of CFO review; agree a sample of intercompany charges to the policy.

Risk: Tax payments and filings are missed or made late, resulting in interest and penalties.
Control objective: Ensure all tax filings and payments are made by their due dates.
Control description: The Tax Manager maintains a compliance calendar of all filing and payment obligations by jurisdiction, monitors completion, and reports status to the CFO monthly. Missed or at-risk deadlines are escalated.
Segregation of duties: Status independently reported to the CFO rather than self-certified without review.
Test of design: Inspect the compliance calendar for completeness of obligations by jurisdiction.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of months; inspect the status report and evidence of escalation of at-risk items.
Population / evidence source: Tax compliance calendar and status reports

Risk: Tax accounts in the general ledger are not reconciled, so misstatements in tax balances go undetected.
Control objective: Ensure tax balances reconcile to supporting computations and filings.
Control description: The Tax Manager reconciles all tax accounts in the general ledger to computations, returns and payments quarterly. Reconciling items are explained and cleared and the reconciliation is reviewed by the Financial Controller.
Segregation of duties: Preparer independent of reviewer.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation template and the accounts covered.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of quarters; verify accuracy of the reconciliation and evidence of review.

Risk: The close is not completed on a controlled basis, so errors are not identified before reporting.
Control objective: Ensure the close is executed completely and on schedule.
Control description: A close calendar and checklist assigns each task, owner and due date. The Financial Controller monitors completion daily through the close and confirms all tasks are complete and signed off before results are released.
Segregation of duties: Task performer and checklist sign-off reviewer are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the close calendar and checklist for completeness of tasks and assignment of owners.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; inspect the completed checklist, sign-offs and any tasks completed late.

Risk: Unauthorised or unsupported journal entries are posted, misstating the financial statements.
Control objective: Ensure journal entries are supported and independently approved before posting.
Control description: All manual journal entries require supporting documentation and electronic approval by a reviewer other than the preparer before posting. The ERP prevents a preparer from approving their own entry.
Segregation of duties: Preparer cannot approve own journal; enforced by system configuration.
Test of design: Inspect the journal workflow configuration confirming preparer and approver must differ.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of manual journals; inspect supporting documentation and approval prior to posting. Test the configuration by attempting self-approval.

Risk: Journals posted outside normal parameters are used to manipulate reported results, including through management override.
Control objective: Ensure high-risk and non-standard journals are identified and scrutinised.
Control description: The Financial Controller reviews a monthly report of high-risk journals, including those posted after the close cutoff, to seldom-used accounts, in round amounts, by unusual users, or above threshold, and documents investigation of each.
Segregation of duties: Reviewer independent of journal preparation; the CFO's own journals are reviewed by the Audit Committee chair.
Test of design: Inspect the criteria defining high-risk journals and confirm the report captures each criterion.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; inspect the report, the investigation documented, and conclusions reached.

Risk: Balance sheet accounts are not reconciled, so errors and unsupported balances persist undetected.
Control objective: Ensure all balance sheet accounts are reconciled and reviewed each period.
Control description: All balance sheet accounts are reconciled monthly to supporting documentation. Reconciliations are reviewed and approved by a reviewer independent of the preparer, with review depth based on account risk rating.
Segregation of duties: Preparer and reviewer are different; the reviewer does not post to the accounts reconciled.
Test of design: Inspect the reconciliation policy, the account risk rating and the review requirements by rating.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of account-months across risk ratings; verify support, accuracy and evidence of timely review.

Risk: Reconciling items are carried forward indefinitely, masking errors or unrecorded transactions.
Control objective: Ensure reconciling items are aged, investigated and cleared.
Control description: Reconciling items are aged on each reconciliation. Items above threshold or older than 60 days are escalated to the Financial Controller with a clearance plan, and progress is monitored monthly.
Segregation of duties: Escalation independent of the preparer of the reconciliation.
Test of design: Inspect the ageing thresholds and escalation criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of reconciliations with aged items; inspect escalation, clearance plans and progress.

Risk: The consolidation is inaccurate, misstating group results and position.
Control objective: Ensure the consolidation is complete and accurate.
Control description: The Group Financial Controller reconciles the consolidation output to submitted entity reporting packs, confirms all entities in scope are included, and reviews consolidation journals for support and approval.
Segregation of duties: Consolidation journals prepared and reviewed by different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the consolidation process, the entity scope listing and the journal approval requirement.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of periods; agree entity packs to the consolidation, confirm scope completeness, and inspect approval of consolidation journals.

Risk: Intercompany balances and transactions do not eliminate, misstating group results.
Control objective: Ensure intercompany balances are matched and eliminated in full.
Control description: Intercompany balances and transactions are matched between entities each period. Unmatched differences above threshold are investigated and resolved before consolidation, and residual differences are approved by the Group Financial Controller.
Segregation of duties: Both entities confirm; neither resolves a difference unilaterally.
Test of design: Inspect the matching process and the tolerance for residual differences.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of periods; inspect the matching report, investigation of differences and approval of residuals.

Risk: Foreign currency translation is applied at incorrect rates or to incorrect balances, misstating results and reserves.
Control objective: Ensure foreign currency translation uses approved rates and correct methodology.
Control description: Exchange rates are loaded from an approved independent source and locked for the period. The Group Financial Controller reviews the translation, confirming closing rates for balance sheet items and average rates for income statement items, and agrees the translation reserve movement.
Segregation of duties: Rate loading and review performed by different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the rate source, the loading process and the translation methodology configuration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of periods; agree rates to the independent source and re-perform the translation reserve movement.

Risk: Significant accounting estimates are biased or unsupported, misstating the financial statements.
Control objective: Ensure significant estimates are supported, challenged and approved.
Control description: Each significant estimate is documented with its methodology, key assumptions and supporting data. The CFO reviews and challenges the assumptions, and the Audit Committee is informed of significant judgements and changes in assumptions.
Segregation of duties: Preparer of the estimate is not the approver; Audit Committee provides independent oversight.
Test of design: Inspect the estimates register and the documentation standard for methodology and assumptions.
Test of operating effectiveness: For a sample of estimates, inspect the documentation, evidence of challenge, and reporting to the Audit Committee.

Risk: The financial statements contain errors or omit required disclosures.
Control objective: Ensure the financial statements are accurate and complete before issue.
Control description: The financial statements are agreed to the consolidation and supporting schedules, a disclosure checklist against the applicable framework is completed and reviewed, and the CFO and Audit Committee approve the statements before issue.
Segregation of duties: Preparer, reviewer and approver are different; Audit Committee approval is independent of management.
Test of design: Inspect the disclosure checklist and the review and approval requirements.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the completed checklist, tie-out of the statements to the consolidation, and evidence of CFO and Audit Committee approval.

Risk: Errors in reported results are not detected because management review is insufficiently precise.
Control objective: Ensure management review of results operates at a level of precision capable of detecting misstatement.
Control description: The CFO reviews results against budget, forecast and prior period at a defined level of disaggregation, investigating variances exceeding defined thresholds and documenting the explanation and corroboration for each.
Segregation of duties: Explanations corroborated to underlying data rather than accepted from the preparer.
Test of design: Inspect the review template, the level of disaggregation and the variance thresholds.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of month ends; inspect the variances investigated, the corroboration obtained and the conclusions documented.

Risk: Users are granted system access beyond what their role requires, enabling unauthorised transactions.
Control objective: Ensure access is granted only on documented authorisation appropriate to the role.
Control description: New user access and changes to entitlements require a request approved by the user's line manager and the application owner before provisioning by IT Security. Access is granted on the basis of predefined roles.
Segregation of duties: Requestor, approver and provisioner are different individuals.
Test of design: Inspect the access request workflow and the role definitions.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of access grants and changes; inspect approval by line manager and application owner prior to provisioning.
Population / evidence source: Access request tickets; system access logs

Risk: Access is not revoked on termination or transfer, leaving active credentials for individuals without a business need.
Control objective: Ensure access is revoked promptly on termination or role change.
Control description: HR notifies IT Security of terminations and transfers through an automated feed. Access is disabled within one business day of the termination date, and IT Security reconciles the HR leaver report to disabled accounts monthly.
Segregation of duties: Reconciliation performed by someone other than the individual disabling accounts.
Test of design: Inspect the HR to IT notification feed and the monthly reconciliation template.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of leavers; inspect the date access was disabled against the termination date. Inspect monthly reconciliations for exceptions.
Population / evidence source: HR leaver reports; account status reports

Risk: Privileged or superuser access is held more widely than necessary, permitting undetected changes to data or configuration.
Control objective: Ensure privileged access is restricted, justified and monitored.
Control description: Privileged accounts are restricted to named individuals with documented business justification approved by the IT Director. Privileged activity is logged and the log is reviewed monthly by a reviewer independent of the account holders.
Segregation of duties: Log reviewer must not hold privileged access to the system reviewed.
Test of design: Inspect the privileged access register, justifications and the logging configuration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the privileged access listing for approval, and a sample of monthly log reviews for evidence of independent review and follow-up.
Sample size guidance: Full listing plus 3 to 5 log reviews

Risk: Accumulated entitlements are not detected because access is never re-examined after it is granted.
Control objective: Ensure user access is periodically recertified by the business.
Control description: Application owners recertify all user access quarterly, confirming continued business need and appropriateness. Access identified as no longer required is revoked within ten business days and completion is tracked centrally.
Segregation of duties: Recertification performed by the business owner, not by IT or by the user.
Test of design: Inspect the recertification procedure, scope of applications and the revocation timeframe.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each quarter, inspect completed recertifications, exceptions identified and evidence that revocations were actioned.

Risk: Weak authentication permits unauthorised access to financially significant systems.
Control objective: Ensure authentication settings meet the security standard.
Control description: Password complexity, length, expiry, lockout and multi-factor authentication settings are configured to the approved security standard on all financially significant systems, and configuration is reviewed annually.
Segregation of duties: Configuration changes require approval separate from the administrator applying them.
Test of design: Compare configured settings on each in-scope system to the approved security standard.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect current configuration screenshots or extracts for each in-scope system and the annual review documentation.

Risk: Changes are migrated to production without authorisation or testing, disrupting processing or corrupting financial data.
Control objective: Ensure changes are tested and approved before migration to production.
Control description: Changes follow the documented change process: requested and approved, developed, tested including user acceptance where applicable, and approved by the change advisory board before migration to production.
Segregation of duties: Developer cannot approve or migrate their own change.
Test of design: Inspect the change management procedure and the approval gates before production migration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of changes; inspect the request, approval, test evidence and pre-migration approval.

Risk: Emergency changes bypass the standard process and are never subsequently reviewed.
Control objective: Ensure emergency changes are justified and retrospectively approved.
Control description: Emergency changes require verbal authorisation at the time and full documentation and retrospective approval by the change advisory board within five business days, with justification for the emergency route.
Segregation of duties: Retrospective approver is not the individual who made the change.
Test of design: Inspect the emergency change procedure and the retrospective approval requirement.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the full population of emergency changes for justification and retrospective approval within the required period.

Risk: Developers hold access to production, enabling unapproved changes to code or data.
Control objective: Ensure development and production environments and access are segregated.
Control description: Development, test and production environments are separate. Developers do not hold write access to production; migration is performed by a separate release function. Exceptions require documented approval and compensating monitoring.
Segregation of duties: This control is the segregation mechanism; exceptions monitored through privileged activity logging.
Test of design: Inspect environment architecture and production access listings for development personnel.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the production access listing for developer accounts and evaluate any approved exceptions and their compensating controls.

Risk: Backups fail or are not recoverable, so financial data cannot be restored after an incident.
Control objective: Ensure backups complete successfully and are recoverable.
Control description: Backups run to the defined schedule and completion is monitored daily, with failures investigated and re-run. Restoration testing is performed at least annually and results documented.
Segregation of duties: Monitoring performed independently of backup job configuration.
Test of design: Inspect the backup schedule, monitoring process and the restoration testing requirement.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of days; inspect backup completion and resolution of failures. Inspect the annual restoration test results.

Risk: Scheduled jobs fail without detection, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate financial processing.
Control objective: Ensure batch job failures are detected and resolved.
Control description: Financially significant batch jobs are monitored on completion. Failures generate an alert, are logged, investigated and re-run, and unresolved failures are escalated to the IT Operations Manager.
Segregation of duties: Job configuration changes approved separately from job execution monitoring.
Test of design: Inspect the job schedule, the list of financially significant jobs and the alerting configuration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of days; inspect the failure log, investigation and resolution of each failure.

Risk: Third parties are engaged without assessment of their financial, operational or integrity risk.
Control objective: Ensure third parties are risk assessed and approved before engagement.
Control description: Prospective third parties undergo due diligence proportionate to their risk tier, covering financial standing, sanctions and adverse media screening, and are approved by the Procurement Director before contracting.
Segregation of duties: Requesting business unit does not perform or approve its own due diligence.
Test of design: Inspect the due diligence procedure and the risk tiering criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of new third parties; inspect the due diligence performed, screening results and approval before contracting.

Risk: Contracts are executed without review, omitting protections over data, audit rights and service levels.
Control objective: Ensure contracts are reviewed and executed under delegated authority.
Control description: Contracts are reviewed by Legal against the approved contracting standards, including data protection, right to audit, service levels and termination, and are executed by an authorised signatory per the delegation of authority.
Segregation of duties: Negotiator does not execute the contract; signature authority held separately.
Test of design: Inspect the contracting standards and the signature authority matrix.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of contracts; inspect legal review and execution by an authorised signatory.

Risk: Controls at a service organisation processing financially significant transactions are ineffective and this is not detected.
Control objective: Ensure assurance is obtained over controls at service organisations.
Control description: For each service organisation supporting a financially significant process, the Financial Controller obtains and reviews the annual SOC 1 Type 2 report, evaluating the opinion, exceptions noted, and the period covered against the reporting period.
Segregation of duties: Review performed by finance rather than by the relationship owner alone.
Test of design: Inspect the register of in-scope service organisations and the review template.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each in-scope service organisation, inspect the SOC 1 report obtained, the documented review, and the assessment of any qualifications or exceptions.

Risk: Complementary user entity controls assumed by the service organisation are not implemented at the entity.
Control objective: Ensure complementary user entity controls are identified and operating.
Control description: The Financial Controller extracts the complementary user entity controls from each SOC 1 report, maps them to controls operating at the entity, and confirms their operating effectiveness. Gaps are remediated and tracked.
Segregation of duties: Mapping reviewed independently of the process owner responsible for the control.
Test of design: Inspect the CUEC mapping methodology and the remediation tracking.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each SOC 1 report, inspect the CUEC listing, the mapping to entity controls and evidence those controls operate.

Risk: Controls at a subservice organisation carved out of the SOC 1 report are not covered by any assurance.
Control objective: Ensure carved-out subservice organisations are identified and addressed.
Control description: For each SOC 1 report using the carve-out method, the Financial Controller identifies the subservice organisations excluded and obtains assurance over them directly or documents the alternative procedures performed.
Segregation of duties: Assessment documented and reviewed rather than assumed covered.
Test of design: Inspect the methodology for identifying carve-outs from SOC 1 reports.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each carve-out identified, inspect the assurance obtained or the alternative procedures documented.

Risk: Third party performance deteriorates without detection, disrupting processes on which reporting depends.
Control objective: Ensure third party performance is monitored against contracted service levels.
Control description: Relationship owners review performance against contracted service levels quarterly for tier one third parties, document issues and escalate persistent underperformance to the Procurement Director.
Segregation of duties: Escalation route independent of the relationship owner.
Test of design: Inspect the monitoring procedure and the tiering that determines review frequency.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of tier one third parties; inspect quarterly performance reviews and evidence of escalation where relevant.

Risk: Ethical standards are not communicated or reinforced, permitting a culture in which misconduct is tolerated.
Control objective: Ensure the code of conduct is communicated and acknowledged.
Control description: The code of conduct is issued to all employees on hire and annually thereafter, with electronic acknowledgement tracked to completion. Non-completion is escalated to the line manager and to HR.
Segregation of duties: Completion tracked centrally rather than self-certified by business units.
Test of design: Inspect the code of conduct, the distribution process and the tracking mechanism.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the annual completion report, the rate achieved and evidence of escalation for non-completion.

Risk: Concerns about misconduct are not reported or are not investigated, allowing fraud to continue undetected.
Control objective: Ensure a whistleblower channel operates and reports are investigated.
Control description: An independently operated whistleblower hotline permits anonymous reporting. Reports are logged, triaged and investigated under a documented protocol, and the Audit Committee receives a summary of all reports and their outcomes each quarter.
Segregation of duties: Hotline operated by an independent provider; reports concerning senior management routed directly to the Audit Committee.
Test of design: Inspect the whistleblower policy, the independence of the provider and the investigation protocol.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the report log and, for a sample, the investigation performed and the outcome. Inspect quarterly Audit Committee reporting.

Risk: The Audit Committee lacks the independence or competence to challenge management effectively.
Control objective: Ensure the Audit Committee is appropriately composed and discharges its responsibilities.
Control description: The Audit Committee comprises independent non-executive directors including at least one with recent and relevant financial experience. It meets at least quarterly against a terms of reference covering financial reporting, internal control, internal audit and external audit, and meets privately with internal and external audit.
Segregation of duties: Committee independent of management; private sessions held without management present.
Test of design: Inspect the terms of reference and the composition against independence and competence criteria.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect minutes for each meeting in the period, confirming coverage of the terms of reference and the holding of private sessions.
Population / evidence source: Audit Committee terms of reference and minutes

Risk: Risks to financial reporting are not identified, so controls are not designed to address them.
Control objective: Ensure risks to financial reporting are identified and assessed periodically.
Control description: Management performs an annual financial reporting risk assessment covering significant accounts, disclosures and processes, considering changes in the business, systems and the external environment. Results drive the scoping of the control framework and are reviewed by the Audit Committee.
Segregation of duties: Assessment challenged by the Audit Committee independently of management.
Test of design: Inspect the risk assessment methodology and its linkage to control scoping.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the annual assessment, the changes made to scope as a result, and evidence of Audit Committee review.

Risk: Fraud risks, including management override, are not specifically assessed or addressed.
Control objective: Ensure fraud risks are assessed and responded to.
Control description: An annual fraud risk assessment identifies fraud schemes relevant to the organisation, the incentives, opportunities and rationalisations present, and maps each to controls. Management override risk is specifically addressed. Results are reported to the Audit Committee.
Segregation of duties: Assessment includes risks arising from management itself and is reviewed by the Audit Committee.
Test of design: Inspect the fraud risk assessment methodology, including coverage of management override.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the annual assessment, the mapping of schemes to controls, and reporting to the Audit Committee.

Risk: Authority is exercised beyond delegated limits because the delegation of authority is outdated or unclear.
Control objective: Ensure the delegation of authority is current and applied.
Control description: The delegation of authority is approved by the Board, reviewed at least annually and on organisational change, and is reflected in system approval workflows. Changes are communicated to affected approvers.
Segregation of duties: Board approves; management cannot expand its own authority.
Test of design: Inspect the delegation of authority, its approval and the linkage to system workflow configuration.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the annual review and Board approval, and reconcile a sample of system approval thresholds to the current matrix.

Risk: Finance personnel lack the competence required, increasing the risk of error in financial reporting.
Control objective: Ensure finance roles are filled by competent individuals whose skills are maintained.
Control description: Finance roles have defined competency requirements applied in recruitment. Performance is evaluated annually against objectives, training needs are identified, and professional qualifications and continuing development are tracked.
Segregation of duties: Evaluation performed by the line manager and moderated independently.
Test of design: Inspect role competency definitions and the evaluation and training processes.
Test of operating effectiveness: Select a sample of finance staff; inspect evidence of evaluation, identified training needs and completion.
Population / evidence source: Job descriptions; performance and training records

Risk: Identified control deficiencies are not remediated, so weaknesses persist across reporting periods.
Control objective: Ensure control deficiencies are evaluated, tracked and remediated.
Control description: Deficiencies from any source are logged, evaluated for severity against defined criteria, assigned an owner and remediation date, and tracked to closure. Status is reported to the Audit Committee quarterly, and significant deficiencies and material weaknesses are escalated on identification.
Segregation of duties: Severity evaluation reviewed independently of the process owner responsible for the deficiency.
Test of design: Inspect the deficiency evaluation criteria and the tracking and escalation process.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the deficiency log, a sample of severity evaluations, evidence of remediation, and quarterly Audit Committee reporting.

Risk: Management overrides controls without detection, circumventing the control framework.
Control objective: Ensure indicators of management override are monitored.
Control description: Monitoring covers indicators of override, including manual journals posted by senior finance management, significant unusual transactions, changes in accounting estimates favouring reported results, and overrides of system-enforced controls. The Audit Committee reviews the results quarterly.
Segregation of duties: Monitoring cannot be performed solely by the individuals whose conduct is being monitored.
Test of design: Inspect the override indicators defined and the reporting route to the Audit Committee.
Test of operating effectiveness: For each quarter, inspect the monitoring performed, items identified, investigation and reporting to the Audit Committee.

Risk: Accounting policies are inconsistently applied because they are not documented or communicated.
Control objective: Ensure accounting policies are documented, current and applied consistently.
Control description: A group accounting manual documents policies for significant transactions, is reviewed annually for changes in the reporting framework, and is communicated to all reporting entities. Departures require Group Financial Controller approval.
Segregation of duties: Departures approved centrally rather than determined locally.
Test of design: Inspect the accounting manual, the annual review process and the departure approval requirement.
Test of operating effectiveness: Inspect the annual review performed, changes made for new requirements, evidence of communication, and any approved departures.
